summary.intent: Execute all plans in GSD phase 68.1 (cipher-box web-client-runtime-integration) using wave-based parallel execution, with the orchestrator staying lean by discovering plans, grouping them into dependency-based waves, and spawning fresh subagents per plan.
summary.outcome: Wave 1 (single plan 68.1-01, owned write-body foundation) completed after its subagent stalled mid-stream and was resumed via SendMessage, landing 5 commits and advancing STATE/ROADMAP/REQUIREMENTS; the orchestrator then passed wave-close gates (build, sdk-core test, drift checks) and kicked off Wave 2 by spawning parallel subagents for plans 02, 03, 05, 07 (deferring plan 08 due to a client.ts overlap with 02), with execution still in progress at transcript end.

repo: cipher-box GSD workflow (.claude/gsd-core/workflows/execute-phase.md) groups phase plans into waves by file-dependency analysis; plans that touch disjoint files run in parallel subagents, while plans sharing a file (e.g. packages/sdk/src/client.ts touched by both plan 02 and 08) are forced into sequential order even within the same wave.
Post-wave gates for this repo include: post-merge build gate, post-merge test gate scoped to sdk-core, and a wave:post drift-check gate, all run before the next wave's dependency/key-links check.
CipherBoxClientConfig.rootWriteKey was made optional (mirroring rootIpnsKeypair) rather than required as plan 68.1-01 implied; self-bootstrap needs both, with host wiring landing in plan 68.1-03.

FolderState.writeKey became a required field during plan 68.1-01; existing test fixtures (helpers.ts, bin.test.ts) had to be updated to use a zero-key legacy path to preserve no-network publish behavior in unit tests.

code.finding: deleteToBin/restoreFromBin publish calls live here, not in client.ts — plan 68.1-01's file list omitted this file even though writeKey/writeChildren threading required touching it.

Removed the 'not implemented — phase 63 (navigation/read fan-out)' stub as part of owned write-body foundation work; this file is also the overlap point forcing plan 08 to run after plan 02 in Wave 2.

workflow: GSD execute-phase has a defined completion-signal fallback for a stalled/stream-interrupted subagent: spot-check filesystem and git state first, then resume the same agent (via SendMessage, not a fresh spawn) so it keeps its full context and can finish uncommitted work.

A resumed subagent can pick back up mid-task and still finish cleanly — the plan 68.1-01 agent stalled after 119 tool calls but ultimately delivered all 3 tasks, 5 commits, and updated tracking docs after resume.

Flag-activation rule pattern: documented optional flags (--wave, --gaps-only, --interactive) are only 'active' if their literal token appears in the phase argument string — avoids the orchestrator inferring intent from the flags' mere documentation.

friction: Wave 1's sole executing subagent stalled mid-stream after 119 tool calls (~23 min), requiring the orchestrator to manually verify state and resume it rather than proceeding automatically.

Reported subagent duration (~28 min including the resume) didn't cleanly match the raw usage stats duration (777110ms ≈ 13 min), suggesting the stall time isn't fully reflected in tool-reported usage metrics.
open_items: Wave 2 execution (plans 02, 03, 05, 07) was still running at transcript end with no results collected yet.
Plan 08 is deferred until after plan 02 completes due to the client.ts file overlap, and hasn't been spawned yet.
